title: 2022 AMC 12A Problem 22
statement: Let \(c\) be a real number, and let \(z_1,\) \(z_2\) be the two complex numbers satisfying the quadratic \(z^2-cz+10=0.\) Points \(z_1,\) \(z_2,\) \(\dfrac{1}{z_1},\) and \(\dfrac{1}{z_2}\) are the vertices of a (convex) quadrilateral \(Q\) in the complex plane. When the area of \(Q\) obtains its maximum value, \(c\) is the closest to which of the following?

solutions.text:
If the roots are non-real, then \(z_1=\sqrt{10}\,e^{i\theta}\) and \(z_2=\overline{z_1},\) since \(z_1z_2=10.\) Then \(\dfrac{1}{z_1}=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{10}}e^{-i\theta}\) and \(\dfrac{1}{z_2}=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{10}}e^{i\theta}.\)

The two vertical sides of this trapezoid have lengths \(2\sqrt{10}\sin\theta\) and \(\frac{2\sin\theta}{\sqrt{10}},\) and their horizontal separation is \((\sqrt{10}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}})\cos\theta.\) Hence its area is \[ \frac{99}{10}\sin\theta\cos\theta =\frac{99}{20}\sin2\theta, \] which is maximized at \(\theta=45^\circ.\)

Then \(c=z_1+z_2\) \(=2\sqrt{10}\cos45^\circ\) \(=2\sqrt5\approx4.47,\) closest to \(4.5.\)

Thus, the correct answer is A.
hints: For real \(c\) with complex roots, \(z_2=\overline{z_1}\) and \(|z_1|=|z_2|=\sqrt{10}\)
The four points form an isosceles trapezoid symmetric about the real axis; write its area in terms of the root’s angle \(\theta\)
